verdict.tagline: A sweeping military vehicle combat game bogged down by an exhausting grind.
for_you_if: you enjoy immersive vehicle combat across land and air
you can pace yourself through a slow progression system
not_for_you_if: you want balanced matches at top tiers
you refuse heavy microtransactions to unlock vehicles
you need external launchers to function without errors

I have been playing war thunder for years, however I do not play on steam. I do, however, have an amount of hours on the game that some would call “Deeply concerning”. All told, I think it is a good game, but recent actions by Gaijin have forced me to write this. I appreciate and enjoy the base-game, but Gaijin is killing their own game without seeing it. Things like the Russian Bias, the fact that premiums are always better, and that they pretty much only work on top tier air is too much. I will give an example: For the 2026 April Fool's event, they added a mode called Nuclear Thunder, which was incredibly fun. The way you played was by spending in-game currency, silver lions, to spawn top-tier jets, even if you didn’t have them. As you can imagine, this appealed to lower-tier players, so we too could experience jets. You can also imagine the excitement I had when I learned they were bringing it back. However they made it so that you had to have the top tier aircraft in order to participate. This is extremely disappointing, but I then looked and realized something even worse. There was only one premium capable of playing the battle rating required for Nuclear Thunder, and its nation: Russia. It is almost like Gaijin wants to alienate the playerbase. I truly believe the game will die if this behavior continues, and hope that the devs can see the light. They are trying to make it so that, in order to have fun, you must spend money to buy broken vehicles. They also refuse to be creative, in that the new vehicles are almost all premium, copy-paste, goated vehicles. The players now have one course of action left. We will rise up. We will force them to make the game playable. But above all, we must not bow to their standards. I pride myself on never having bought a premium or premium subscription. I request all of you to follow in this, so that we may force their hand. This is simply the only option.

The game has good foundations when tank games are concerned. If we were to consider the big three tank games, aka World of Tanks, War Thunder, and Armored Warfare, this game by far got its bases the best. However despite having strong foundations with the mechanics and such, i still CANNOT recogmend this game. I've been playing this game since years, despite my low playtime here on steam. I started out on console. Been playing this game since Italy came into the game (which was around 2017).

Let me list the reasons why i cannot recogmend:

The grind - Been painful for a long time now, however nowadays pretty much all nations have grown large. Back then the grind wasnt that big of an issue since you could choose a smaller nation to grind, however nowadays there are NO small nations anymore. Everything has been bloated with copy-paste vehicles. Even with premium account, and a premium vehicle, it still takes a long time to reach higher tiers. (free to play, upwards of a year to reach your first top tier)

Copy paste vehicles - There are a lot of vehicles that have been added to many nations... of course, realisticly, a lot of nations have bought equipment from other nations, but the amount of copy paste vehicles by now is just hurting the game. There are certain vehicles that basicly every nation has by now. The best example for this is the sherman. All nations have a sherman in at least some shape or form. 

Now back to higher tiers - The game is severely imbalanced. Close air-support in ground realistic battles (the mode that you will mostly be playing) has always been an issue. You can bring in a plane for unreasonably small amount of points, and with a plane, the tanks on the ground cannot do much against you, even anti-aircraft players will mostly be at a disadvantage against you. Helicopters are another can of worms that is a similar story, so i wont get into that too deeply.

AI usage - For certain vehicle skins. This is huge. For those who dont know, the deve…

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the vehicle progression and tech tree grind as excessively slow, requiring substantial time investment or spending money.

citations.review_text:
Too much predatory tactics to drain your money.
EVERYTHING in this game has some sort of monetization to it. Premium vehicles, premium account, battle pass, another like 2 currencies that are only useful with spending real money. Also, those premium vehicles cost like 70 to 80 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dollars, like what the hell? For this amount of money i could buy a whole library of games that are better, and have developers that actually care about their playerbase.

Progression system is almost non-existent, you play like 12 rounds that take 10-15 minutes for one vehicle, just to know. There are like 500 of them!!! You need like 3 hours (of winning, bcs you get almost nothing from loosing) to just earn enough currency and research points to buy ONE vehicle.

Combat is not as bad, i just, dont like it. You usually are always 1-shot away from returning to Steam and uninstalling the game and giving it negative review. But the real problem i have with combat is the matchmaking, the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ MATCHMAKING. You pick team of vehicles with average 3.0 and you end up fighting sometimes 4.3, which really, and like really sucks. BTW the average rating is also stupid, even though it looks like it is average rating of your vehicles, its actually just your highest rated vehicle with maybe like -0.3 to not make it tooooo suspicious.

The only redeeming quality are the graphics i guess, if you have strong enough PC for the highest settings(I dont have that strong of PC so idc about this factor that much).

Oh and cherry on top, when they update the game (which happens like once in 3 months), you cant tell a differce between before and after the update. But somehow the size of the update is like 6-10GB. Seriously where is the content?!? Because except of the new battle pass, there is nothing.

In summary, dont download this game. There are other Military Multiplayer games like World of Tanks, World of Warships, etc...(even tho these two examples arent that better)
Oversized Nothing-ad…

A very long grind experience I would not recommend at all, this forces people to open their wallets to play the game, which I understand as a free-to-play game there should be some way to earn money, but making life tough for free-to-play players is not the way. The matchmaking is also horrendous; in order to reduce queue times, they include higher and better vehicles with you up by 1.0 BR, which causes some vehicles to not even have a fighting chance, and a good change needs to be made to repair this because it is not right trying to fight all-aspect missiles with no countermeasures. Lastly, regarding the game mode itself, I personally don't really care about historic matches, but the player counts per match are frustrating; at top tier where planes can carry up to 14 missiles, playing a 16v16 creates an incredible amount of missiles in the air, making it absolute hell. I understand that nobody wants to fly for 10 minutes just to die and go back to the lobby, so instead of increasing the map size, they should just reduce the player count to something like a 6v6 and spread the teams out in the corners. While there are complaints by other players about premium vehicles and copy-paste slop, I think this isn't as big of an issue as the ones I have stated above since mine affect gameplay much more directly. For context, I used to use the War Thunder launcher directly so I have around 900 hours and have reached top tier in two nations, and while the problems I have listed are specifically for Air Realistic Battles because I do not play tanks, I assume some of these issues might apply to tanks as well.

I want so badly to like this game but it's clear that Gaijin only cares about money and sabotages the actual experience to get it. There is literally nothing like this game which is so unfortunate because that let's Gaijin run a MONOPOLY on their experience since nothing else even comes close. It does so many things well but for every thing it does well, it does 25 things WRONG and most of those wrong things feel terrible to experience. 

TLDR: [spoiler]This game has so much going right for it, but the negatives of the gameplay, learning experience, the insane grind and the down right disgusting levels of corporate greed force you to either fork over hundreds of dollars to stay competitive (Or even break even), or literally spend the rest of your life playing only this game. 
I would stay far away from this game if you can. Play literally any other war game, I promise you'll have a better time and save money. [/spoiler]

[h3] I'll start with the positives [/h3]

[list]
    [*] The game is obviously [strike] Very [/strike] Mostly realistic with its simulation. Your weapon and plane matter a LOT which makes choosing planes very cool

    [*] The variety of vehicles is insane. In my 100 hours I didn't even come close to running out of content to work towards. I barely even scratched the surface

    [*] The gameplay offers a variety and a mix of playstyles. Just in aviation there's multiple different classes of planes that serve many roles. If you want a mix of naval and aerial or a bit of ground and aerial, you can do that.

    [*] Learning this game can be super rewarding. There is so much in depth simulation for each aircraft that you can almost learn how to actually fly just by playing this game

    [*] Arcade and realistic can both be fun, although realistic air is a bit too unforgiving. It's definitely a playstyle and rewarding to get kills but it feels awful to fly for 15 minutes after being in queue for 4 just to get one tapped out of nowhere
[/list]

[h3] No…

Yk, I played this as a new player and put plenty of hours in the game to the point that i should feel like I'm really progressing. but im not. Obviously I'm not saying I should be able to get to top tier super fast, but I also shouldn't still be at a ~4.0 BR. Sure I didn't purely grind 1 nation, but its bad game design to force the player to use the same tools for a unrealistic amount of time before they get new toys and do the same thing. I wanted to reach an ok BR so some of the people I'm friends with would play with me and all of use have a fun time. But, since none of them want to play from reserve to 3.0 Br, I'm often stuck by myself. The gameplay at first isn't bad. But after awhile, its the same thing for the 1000th time. I never got upset at the game or rage when I lose because 1, I don't get ticked off at games, and 2, I got exhausted before I would even get irritated. But the part that was really the final nail in the coffin, is the ai slop. A game that uses ai to promote it's game is probably one of the biggest deal breakers for me. I hate how every company uses ai like its some trump card. When in reality, you're simply showing me how much you are in it for the money than the actual passion for the game. Not including how harmful ai is especially in the art community

If you don't want to read that yap session (Don't blame you), to put simply: War thunder fails at good progression for new players, its extremely redundant gameplay, and uses ai to promote it's game and uses ai art in game. With all of these to consider, if you're a new player looking at warthunder, if you want to play the game without spending a dime and don't have anyone to play low BRs with you, I do not recommend this game

games great just so openly pay to grind, it took me 45 hours as a new player to get a 4.0 lineup as usa, bought a russian 12.0 and got 5.0 lineup in a completly new tech tree in just 12 hours, grinding for free to play players is just terrible but managble if you have 5 hours a day to play the game

This game is a very special one. Technically the game is "free" but if you even thought about using a plane made within the last 15 years, have fun grinding for 2 hours a day for a year and a half. Without premium and realistic battles, this game is genuinely impossible to grind. Arcade is a waste of time. And the performance of this game!!! I have a very impressive spec sheet on my pc, and I have overclocked my GPU. I run at 97-100% utilization consistently and without frame gen, I cant get over 80fps. Cyberpunk 2077 runs better on my system and I have max settings with some ray tracing. Im not even running max settings on War Thunder.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the in-game economy and progression grind as extremely slow, demanding, and heavily incentivizing purchases.

citations.review_text:
I cannot decently recommand this game to anyone. I spent enough time and money on it and came to despise what was a very promising free-to-play game that now has become a predatory cash grab full of AI-slop and poor balancing incenting players to pay to overcome frustration.

I've been playing regularly since 2020 and noticed a drastic drop in quality each update. Most of the vehicles added in recent years are copy/pastes and balancing is all over the roof to push players to buy the last OP thing that came out not to suffer from it, but to have fun by making other players suffer until it is nerfed into oblivion or almost never adressed at all. The fun you can have in this game is mostly based on a FOMO trend hidden behind a paywall (that increasingly got more expsensive with vehicles costing ~80€). The grind is quite unoticeable in the first tiers to lure the player and hook them into one of the most grindy experience I have ever had in a videogame.

About the community, I haven't played a single match without witnessing someone typing racist stuff in chat or even litteral neo-nazi emblems on vehicles. Going from Azov battalion to creative recreations of swastikas. It's a game about tanks, I know some of the players are degenerates but moderation feels non-existent or quite permissive in the wrong way.

I've had fun for a while, but don't let yourself get fooled by the many adds Gaijin Entertainment spreads on the Internet : the game is an unfinished mess where issues are not worked on anymore since Gaijin is more focused on adding new stuff (that adds more imbalance and bugs) than fixing game breaking experience/flaws or working on decent moderation.

War Thunder is a free-to-play game that will cost you your time and mental health, until you eventually give up and spend more money on microtransactions than you would on a paid game. This is a game with the most unrealistic realism, because despite being promised realism, it is simply not there—just like the balance.The tech tree here is longer than the line to Putin's mother in her youth. To get to the modern Abrams or Leopards, you have to go through all the circles of hell. You will spend months driving around in rusty buckets. And when you finally unlock that long-awaited top-tier tank, you'll find out that its stock configuration doesn't even include... a repair kit or a fire extinguisher. In other words, your crew is a suicide squad; upon the very first hit to their tracks, they will just stand in the middle of a field and sadly watch their tank burn because you need to research the fire extinguisher for another 20 matches.The exact kind of game where you get spawn-killed and then press "Find Match" in the hope that it won't happen again, but you have no other choice.

War Thunder offers a military vehicle experience that no other game offers. That being said, the in game economy is terrible. The grind is absolutely unbearable and it is almost impossible for a free-to-play player to have unlock even a third of the vehicles in game in under 5 years. It is totally unreasonable for Gaijin to expect someone to spend 5-10 hours, sometimes even more, researching a single vehicle. Even if you do spend money on this game to buy premium time and/or premium vehicles, you will still spend an unbelievable amount of time tying to get to top tier on just one nation. Not to mention that the game needs serious balancing rework. In Air RB especially, the battle rating is super compressed and makes it almost unplayable for me. I love this game and have been playing for years because it is very fun to play realistic and well made models of historical vehicles. But this game has so many issues that I can't justify telling someone to play it.

War Thunder is a game with an incredibly ambitious concept and an impressive amount of content, but after spending a significant amount of time playing it, I found that its strengths are consistently overshadowed by frustrating design decisions. While it excels in historical authenticity, vehicle variety, and realistic combat mechanics, the overall experience becomes increasingly difficult to enjoy due to its progression system, balance issues, and heavy emphasis on monetization.

One of the game's greatest achievements is its enormous collection of military vehicles. Players have access to hundreds of aircraft, tanks, helicopters, and naval vessels from numerous nations, many of which are recreated with an impressive level of detail. The sound design, vehicle models, and damage mechanics demonstrate the amount of effort that has gone into creating an immersive battlefield. At its best, War Thunder delivers tense, rewarding encounters where positioning, map knowledge, and tactical decision-making genuinely matter. Those moments are exciting and memorable, showing the potential of what the game can be.

Unfortunately, these positive aspects are often overshadowed by an exhausting progression system. Advancing through the technology trees becomes increasingly time-consuming as players reach higher ranks. Research costs continue to increase, vehicle modifications require substantial amounts of experience, and earning enough in-game currency to purchase and maintain vehicles can become a challenge. While the game can technically be enjoyed without spending money, progression frequently feels slow enough that premium accounts, premium vehicles, and various boosters appear less like optional conveniences and more like practical necessities. This creates the impression that the game prioritizes extending player engagement and encouraging purchases rather than providing consistently rewarding progression.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that matchmaking suffers from battle rating compression, placing vehicles against vastly superior opponents.

citations.review_text:
First off, the game is unfortunately the only thing like it on the market, because if it wasn't, some smart Devs could easily knock this game off it's pedestal by doing what this game does but actually caring about balance and more then COD style team death match gameplay.

Just some of the major issues this game has.

Matchmaker bracket compression, known in game as Battle ratings (BR) are a two up two down system where you can end up facing vehicles that vastly outperform your chosen vehicle and have been a constant issue since the games inception. The developers insistence that decompression would effect queue times has been their go to response from community demand that they actually decompress the game to bring about something resembling balance and ♥♥♥♥ the queue times have largely been ignored. -- This creates pockets of BR brackets for nations that are practically unplayable because of poor balancing.

-$80 premium vehicles that are placed too low in the matchmaking bracket with broken features that get milked until sales dry up. Further compounding the above issue.

-The developers taking a very inconsistent attitude to implementation of the vehicles in game. Adding things like missiles to some aircraft that were only ever tested on them but not deployed operationally while others will at times not get missiles they actually used for "balance," despite the game being a generally unbalanced mess that gives you the impression no one on the dev team actually plays the game they make.  

-Game modes - The base game is basically COD style team death match in tanks or planes (Naval is a thing but practically abandoned and ignore.) There are game modes that were teased back in 2014 (Enduring Confrontation) that they at most had a few tests on than largely ignored. -- For tanks this means modern battle tanks in what is essentially 1.5km square maps for a good chunk of top BR cod style twitch death matches with the occasional camper sitting and waiting for people t…

I am mostly free to play (I pay for premium) who plays in spare time after work, after my kids go to sleep. The grind is slow and hard, there are a ton of excellent players who will wreck you over and over again unless you have a good mentor to teach you the ways of the game.  Balance barely exists. It practically does not exist above 8.0 (thankfully i'm not there yet). Due to balancing issues and BR compression this game is terrible for new players and the Premium vehicles (great for grinding) are a mix of OP and copy paste vehicles between tech trees (copy paste is better by far than P2W). I would not recommend to new players until they can decompress BRs, introduce era-separated matches, make aircraft cost more to spawn in GROUND RB, and/or reduce the pain of grinding.

I don’t play War Thunder on Steam anymore, I’ve been using the Gaijin launcher for a long time, but I still play it regularly. And like a lot of people, I’ve seen the community finally start speaking out about how far downhill the game has gone. Honestly, I agree with pretty much all of it. Gaijin Entertainment has become incredibly lazy when it comes to supporting the game.

One of the biggest creators, TheCodMineMan, who’s actually part of Gaijin’s partner program, has openly called out the state of the game. And now it’s not just him. Pretty much every major creator is talking about it: PhlyDaily, OddBawz, Spookston, all of them agree something is seriously wrong.

The issues are hard to ignore: overpriced pay to win premium vehicles, tons of copy-paste vehicles, and underwhelming event rewards that aren’t worth the grind. There’s also a lack of meaningful game modes,older, more enjoyable modes were removed and never replaced, and new ones just get removed as if they're just nothing, while FOMO tactics and even AI-generated decals have started creeping in.

Naval feels pointless, A waste of money, and useless, because barely anyone plays it, and there really is no reason to play it, when You can just go play something better at this point such as World of Warships, that has so much love and effort put into it.

And faction matchmaking has become random and unrealistic, which kills immersion compared to how the game used to be.

Back in 2013–2015, War Thunder actually felt unique. Now it just feels neglected, and it really shows.

The difference now is that the people speaking out aren’t just random players, they’re creators inside Gaijin’s own program. That means this can’t just be ignored. If nothing changes, Gaijin risks losing a huge part of its player base, along with revenue and reputation from all the negative attention.

Gaijin, please actually listen to what Your playerbase and Community are speaking about, Please do not neglect this moment …
